Start here

Everything for the new omarchebbo.com, in one file

A working demo of the new site, the full build spec, every change, and the reasons behind each decision. Everything here was designed phone-first, because most visitors arrive from Instagram and TikTok on a phone.

How to use this file

  1. Open Live demo. It's the new site, working, built into this file. Tick Review in the demo's top bar to see a note on each section: what was wrong, what changed, and a screenshot of the original.
  2. Read Build spec, starting with "Fix before launch". It says how each part should look and behave, plus the phone rules, the Sanity setup and the emails.
  3. Work through All changes and tick each item as you build it. Ticks are saved in this browser.
  4. Check Waiting on Omar for content that's still coming, and Context & decisions for the reasons behind the choices.

Key facts

Site
Next.js + Sanity. Staging: stg.omarchebbo.com
Pages
Home (a hub) · The book · Reviews · Start here · Free guides · Videos · My story · Shop · Questions · Privacy & terms (draft)
Payment
Whish (Whish Pay). The buyer goes to Whish to confirm the payment, then comes back. Confirm orders on the server from Whish's callback.
Products
The Introduction: $9.99 PDF, sent by email right after payment · Full memoir ebook: $14.99 pre-order · Hardcover: $35 pre-order, free delivery, signed or unsigned · Bundle (introduction + signed hardcover): $41, was $44.99 (price to confirm)
Release
The full memoir (ebook and hardcover) comes out in June 2027
Refunds
All sales are final
Donation
All net profits go to the dialysis unit at AUBMC in Beirut, after basic creation and processing costs. The first donation is already made; the hospital's signed confirmation is a one-page document on Google Drive (link to come).
Free guides
Two Arabic PDFs, downloaded directly (no email needed). Two more are "Coming soon".
Contact
hello@omarchebbo.com · Instagram, TikTok and YouTube: @omar_organtransplants
Donor link
nodlb.org (how to register as an organ donor in Lebanon)

Build spec

How each part should look and behave

The full developer handoff. Port the demo's behavior into the Next.js components; the demo code isn't meant to be dropped in as is.

Start here

Every change below is already built and working in a clickable demo of the site. Use it as the reference for layout and behavior, and port it into the Next.js components; the demo code isn't meant to be dropped in as is.

  • Demo, best opened on a phone: Demo + Original Website. Tick Review in the top bar to see a note on each section: what was wrong on the live site, what changed, and a screenshot of the original.
  • Code: GitHub repo omarchebbo97-coder/btbtp-media, branch ccr-72a2b1ad-6o2sbb, folder web-demos/demo-original-mixed/ (one index.html plus img/). Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no libraries.
  • Background: Site review has the section-by-section findings; Design benchmarks compares the site with five design galleries.
  • Jump links in the demo: #hero, #book-sec, #both, #start, #guides, #shorts, #blog, #journey, #about, #faq, #donor, #news. #book and #shop open those pages.
  • Colors: keep the current palette (slate, gold, cream, ink). The color dots in the demo's top bar exist only for comparing; the top bar itself is not part of the site. Use the colors in a 60 / 30 / 10 split: cream about 60% (main background), slate about 30% (secondary), gold as the accent. Slate sections: news strip, book section, story timeline, the first quote band ("Dialysis doesn't restore life…"), and footer (the homepage's short story and newsletter are cream), plus a slate panel behind the book cover on the book page and behind each shop product picture. Gold: every main button (including the shop's "Add to cart" and "Pre-order"), the "always choose the sky" quote band, the "Become a donor" section, the timeline line and dates, the shop badges and the review stars. Labels are in sentence case (no all-caps), and headings don't highlight a single phrase. Measured in the demo: homepage 54 / 36 / 10 on a phone and 58 / 33 / 9 on a computer; book page and shop about 63–66 / 31–34 / 3.
  • Placeholders: anything marked "Omar to confirm" in the demo is waiting on content or a decision (see Waiting on Omar).

Site structure

The homepage is now a home page instead of one long scroll. At first look it tells a visitor three things: who Omar is, what's here for them (his book, and free help for patients and families), and why it matters (net profits go to dialysis care at AUBMC). Anything that was repeated got its own page, reached by a button. On a phone the homepage went from about 12,500px to 5,500px tall.

  • Homepage (#home): hero, book section, Free help (four buttons), My story: the short version, Before you buy (3 questions and "All questions"), Become a donor, newsletter, footer. Two more pages: Reviews (#reviews: real reviews only, and a form to leave one) and Questions (#faq: all 8 questions).
  • Start here (#start): the body map ("Tap the body"), "Your situation" and the blog posts. Ends with buttons to Free guides and Videos.
  • Free guides (#guides): the guide cards in a grid, then "Not sure which guide? Start here" and Videos.
  • Videos (#videos): all the shorts in a grid (2 across on phones, 4 on tablets, 6 on desktop), "All videos on YouTube ↗", then Start here and Free guides.
  • My story (#story): About ("Hi, I'm Omar.", then the "Who I am · 1 min" video picture), the timeline, the slate quote band, the before/after sliders, the gold quote band, then "It's all in the book." with "Read the first page" and "Invite me to speak ↗".
  • Privacy & terms (#privacy): a plain-language draft for Omar to approve, linked in the footer.
  • Book page and Shop: unchanged.

Every new page starts with "← Home" and ends with buttons to the other free resources, so there's no dead end. A link to a section on another page (for example #journey or #blog) opens that page and scrolls to the section. The sticky buy bar only shows on the homepage and the book page.

Visitor paths:

  • Supporter from Instagram: "Read the first page" → preview → "Keep reading — $9.99" → checkout → Whish. A reader who finished the introduction: "Leave a review" → the Reviews form.
  • Patient or family: "Free help" → Start here, Free guides, Videos or Posts.
  • Curious about Omar: "The short version" → "Read my story" → "Read the first page".
  • Event organizer: My story → "Invite me to speak".

Book page, shop, cart and checkout

Buying takes one tap from anywhere on the site, and the cart ends in a full checkout: Cart, Details, Payment, Order confirmed.

Book page (#book)

  • Remove the quantity picker. Two buttons: "Buy now — $9.99" (heartbeat; fills, then opens the cart) and "Add to cart" (the cover flies into the cart icon and the count bumps). Revamp: "Buy now" and every "Get your copy" go straight to the checkout details step (one item doesn't need a cart step; "← Back to cart" stays). Once there are 3 approved reviews, two of them show right under "Buy now". Further down: "Questions before you buy" (how do I get the book after paying, how do I pay, can I read it on my phone, then "All questions") and "Read it already? Leave a review". On phones these buttons sit right under the price, above "What's inside", with a smaller cover (about 160px wide), so "Buy now" is on the first screen. The link above the cover says "← Back" and returns to where the visitor came from, keeping their place on the homepage ("← Back to the shop" when they came from the shop, "← Home" when they landed on the book page directly).
  • Under the description, a numbered "What's inside": Dialysis at fifteen, the only teenager in the ward · The panic attacks and the silence no one prepares you for · The post-transplant shock no one talks about · Making peace with a body of borrowed parts (all from the introduction).
  • "Digital · PDF · Read in one sitting" and "Sent to your email right after payment.", then "Preview the first page", the "Where the money goes" box with the verified badge, and a short "Good to know" box.
  • "You might also like": three cards with their own pictures; titles wrap to two lines instead of being cut off.

Cart and checkout (side drawer, full screen on phones)

  1. Cart: items with their pictures, quantity only for physical items, Remove, subtotal. Below them, "Free guides · download" with a "Download" button for each guide, shown in an empty cart too. Guides download directly and are never cart items. Under each item, its delivery line ("Digital · sent by email", "Pre-order · by email in June 2027", "Pre-order · ships June 2027 · free delivery"); the footer sums them up instead of "Shipping is added at checkout".
  2. Details: progress bar (Cart · Details · Payment), order summary, the email ("for your receipt and download link" only when the introduction is in the order), a delivery address for hardcover orders (full name, phone, city or area, street and building), and one line per item on when it arrives, ending with "All sales are final, no refunds." A missing or wrong field shows a message right under it, not a pop-up. Button "Continue to payment — $X".
  3. Payment: total and receipt email, "Deliver to" and "Delivery: Free" for hardcovers, a "Pay with Whish" box ("You'll go to Whish to confirm the payment with your Whish account, then come straight back here for your receipt"), and "Pay $X with Whish", which shows "Opening Whish…" and sends the buyer to Whish. "Back to details" keeps everything typed.
  4. Order confirmed: "Thank you!", Download the PDF (only when the introduction was bought), "Your ebook arrives by email in June 2027", "Your hardcover ships in June 2027 to <city>, with free delivery", the link to the signed AUBMC document, then "Get my monthly letter" (goes to the sign-up) and "Back to the site".
  • Payment is with Whish (Whish Pay). Use its redirect checkout: create the payment on the server, send the buyer to Whish, and confirm the order only from Whish's callback, never from the browser alone. It needs a Whish Business account and works in USD. Check with Whish whether buyers outside Lebanon, or without a Whish account, can pay.
  • "Get your copy" opens the cart straight away when the book is already in it, without replaying the fill. It is the one buy label across the site: header, phone menu, book section, About, buy bar and empty cart (the book page keeps "Buy now — $9.99"). The introduction is a PDF only, no EPUB, and nothing says "instant download": it is sent by email.

Header and navigation

The header stays at the top while scrolling (sticky), and links to sections leave room for it so headings are never hidden under it. Desktop header links: The book · Reviews · Start here · Free guides · Videos · My story · Shop (the logo goes home); Blog, Gallery and Contact move to the phone menu and the footer. Between 900 and 1150px wide the links move into the menu. The header's "Get your copy" is an outlined button, so the gold one in the hero leads. On phones 420px and wider it shows in the header too (narrower phones have the sticky buy bar), and the header gets a soft shadow once the page scrolls. In the demo, links that open another site show a small ↗; on the live site Blog, Gallery and Contact are Omar's own pages, so they open in the same tab without it. Three things are added around the header.

  • News strip above the header: one line, one piece of news at a time, announcing something the hero doesn't already offer: the newest short ("New · Short: Why are bananas banned on dialysis? · Watch →", opening the video viewer), and once the signed AUBMC document is ready, "My first donation to AUBMC dialysis → See it". Slate background, gold link, a close button. Once closed, remember it for that visitor. The text should be editable in Sanity.
  • Full-screen phone menu: big serif links (Home, The book, Reviews, Start here, Free guides, Videos, My story, Shop, then smaller FAQ, Blog, Gallery and Contact), a gold dot and aria-current="page" on the current page, a small ↗ on links that open another page. At the bottom: "Get your copy", "Get the monthly letter →" and the Instagram, TikTok and YouTube icons. Links slide in one after another when it opens.
  • Cart count: a number on the cart icon whenever the cart has items; it bumps when something is added.

Mobile requirements

Most visitors arrive from Instagram and TikTok on a phone, so mobile is the priority. The demo passes all of these at 320, 390 and 414px; every page of the live site should too.

Content model in Sanity

The site already serves its images from Sanity, so the new sections should be filled from Sanity too, letting Omar add videos, guides and donations without code changes. Suggested fields:

Content typeFields to addUsed by
Short video (existing)organs (heart, liver, blood, old kidneys, new kidney, bladder, dialysis), situations (on dialysis, waiting, after transplant, family), priority (pinned first per organ), titleEn (English line under the Arabic title)Body map, Start here, Shorts row
Blog post (existing)organs, situations, its own cover imageBody map, Start here, Blog
Free guide (new)title (Arabic), description (Arabic), page count, cover image, PDF file, status (available or coming soon), organsFree guides section, cart, body map
Donation (new)date, recipient (AUBMC dialysis unit), amount (optional), document link (Google Drive, view-only) or file, signed by (names and roles)Where the money goes, document pop-up, FAQ
Reader review (new)quote, first name, city, rating (optional, 1–5), product, consent, approved, date. The Reviews form creates an unapproved review (add a honeypot field and a rate limit against spam).Reviews page, book section swipe row, under "Buy now" (the blocks and any count show only with 3 or more approved)
Timeline moment (new)date or label, title, one line, photo, orderStory timeline
Product (existing)own image, "what's included" list, badge (Start here, Best value), limited stock (show "Only X left" only when on)Shop, book page, cart
Site settingsnews strip text, link and on/off; donation goal; "Now" line textNews strip, money box, hero

The body map shows each organ's items sorted by priority, then newest; the top 3 show first, "See all" shows the rest (or links to the videos page filtered by that organ).

EmailSent whenMain content
Order confirmationRight after paymentThe introduction PDF download button, links to the free guides, receipt, where the money goes with a link to the signed document; for pre-orders, June 2027

Context & decisions

Who the site is for, and why it's built this way

About Omar and the site

  • Omar Chebbo is a transplant survivor with 3 organ transplants. His dad gave him part of his liver in 2006. He went on dialysis in March 2013, at fifteen, and spent eleven years in the chair. A new kidney from his brother Amine came on 13 June 2024.
  • He's the author of the memoir Beyond the Body, Beyond the Pain. Its introduction is out first, as a $9.99 PDF. The full memoir (ebook and hardcover) comes out in June 2027.
  • He posts short videos in Arabic with English subtitles (@omar_organtransplants on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube) and writes free guides about lab tests for kidney and transplant patients.
  • The current site, stg.omarchebbo.com, is built with Next.js and Sanity. It has a homepage, book page, shop, blog, gallery and contact page.

Who visits

  • Mostly people on phones, coming from his Instagram and TikTok. That's why every page was designed and checked phone-first.
  • Patients on dialysis, people waiting for a transplant or just after one, and their families. Most are in Lebanon and many read Arabic.
  • Supporters who want to read his story, and help the dialysis unit that cared for him.

What the site needs to do

  • Sell the introduction. Net profits go to the dialysis unit at AUBMC in Beirut, and the first donation is already made.
  • Help patients for free: the guides, the shorts, the body map and the situation buttons in "Start here".
  • Grow the monthly letter list.
  • Encourage organ donor registration in Lebanon (nodlb.org).

Decisions and why

  • One buy label: "Get your copy"The site had five different buy labels. Not "Donate": people are buying a book, and only net profits go to AUBMC. The book page keeps "Buy now — $9.99".
  • The homepage is a hub, not everything at onceIt was about 12,500px on a phone and showed the same guides, videos and posts in several places (the body map, the guide cards, the shorts row, the blog). Now it answers who Omar is, what's here (the book and free help) and why it matters (profits to dialysis care), and every repeated thing has its own page behind a button. It's now about 5,500px.
  • Reviews: real ones onlyReviews are the top priority, and they only work if they're real. Each review shows a first name and a city, no count shows until there are three approved ones, and nothing is invented. Until then the site invites readers to leave the first reviews. A clearly labeled preview shows the layout with template text.
  • The heading is a statement, the name is small"Eleven years on dialysis. Three transplants. This is what nobody told me." Visitors from social media don't know the name yet, so the facts lead and replace the row of numbers. Under the buttons, a link to the first donation's signed confirmation is proof people can check.
  • "Buy now" goes straight to checkoutOne item doesn't need a cart step. "Add to cart" still goes to the cart, and "Back to cart" stays in checkout.
  • Hero buttons: "Read the first page" and "Free help""Read my story" led to a price, and "Watch the videos" sent followers back to YouTube. The first screen now offers two clear choices instead of four: one for readers and supporters, one for patients and families.
  • No pop-up asking for an email on arrivalOn a phone it covers Omar's name before visitors know who he is. The guides are offered in the news strip and their own section instead.
  • Free guides: direct download, Arabic onlyOmar's choice. The guides are in Arabic, so the cards are too. The email list grows from the monthly letter and the "Coming soon" cards.
  • Delivery by email, all sales final, PDF onlyOmar's choice. Nothing says "instant download", because the file is sent by email.
  • Payment with WhishIt works for a business in Lebanon. Whish's online checkout is described as cardless (buyers pay from a Whish account), so check with Whish whether buyers outside Lebanon can pay.
  • Showing that the donation is realThe first donation is shown with a link to the hospital's signed one-page confirmation. The progress bar and amounts stay hidden until there are real numbers, rather than showing example figures.
  • "Who I am" video from YouTube, loaded only on tapThe photo stays, with a play button on it, so the page stays light. A silent looping video was dropped because it would load YouTube's player for every visitor.
  • Gentle animation onlyAnimations are welcome "but not too much". All motion stops with Reduce Motion. The IV-bag drip on the cover was removed, and the body-map characters bob three times, then rest.
  • No fake scarcityThe "Only 2 left" and "Only 3 left" badges were removed.
  • Keep the current colorsSlate, gold, cream and ink. The color dots in the demo's top bar were only for comparing options.

Facts to keep consistent

  • 3 organ transplants · 11 years on dialysis (2013 to 2024) · 26+ years of the journey.
  • Dialysis began in March 2013, at fifteen (not fourteen or sixteen).
  • The donation sentence, everywhere: "All net profits go to the dialysis unit at AUBMC in Beirut, the place that held my life for years, after basic creation and processing costs."
  • The "Now" line: "The full memoir comes out in June 2027."

Images in the demo (img/)

  • Photos: grad (hero), aftertx and dialysis (timeline, short story), sky, fistula, diving, catheter, shooting (before/after sliders, timeline), flu and armpost (blog), cover (book). The My story page uses the "Who I am" video picture instead of a photo.
  • Shorts thumbnails: short_<YouTube id>.webp (12).
  • Body map characters: c_*.webp. Guide covers: g_blood, g_aftertx. Product pictures: p_intro, p_ebook, p_hard, p_bundle (480×600, transparent). Timeline: t_*.webp.
  • Original-site screenshots for the Review notes: orig_*.webp (reference only, not for the site).

How the demo was checked

  • No sideways scrolling on any of the 10 pages (home, book, shop, Reviews, Questions, Start here, Free guides, Videos, My story, Privacy) at 320, 360, 390, 414, 768, 1024 and 1366px wide.
  • The review form: an empty send shows a red message under each missing field, a short note shows how many characters are left, and a complete review shows the thank-you message and is not published.
  • At phone widths: every button and link at least 44×44px, and no text under 12px.
  • Each path clicked through: buying up to "Order confirmed" (introduction only, and hardcover with an address), each Free help button, the body map (a guide item opens the guides page and highlights the guide; a story item opens the timeline), the video viewer, the timeline pop-up, the Back button and keyboard use.

Demo-only, don't build

  • The dark top bar (color dots, Review) and the Review notes.
  • "Prototype: no payment is taken", and messages that start with "Demo:".
  • Blog, Gallery and Contact opening the staging site in a new tab with ↗. On the live site they're Omar's own pages, so they open in the same tab.

Prepared for Omar Chebbo's developer. Questions about content: hello@omarchebbo.com.
